title: Quantization error in a dot product: aligned vs independent
why: It shows the structural difference between worst-case aligned error accumulation and independent zero-mean error accumulation over N terms.
notes: Two bars or columns compare the aligned worst case and the independent-error standard deviation. The horizontal axis is accumulation regime; the vertical axis is output error magnitude. Labels come directly from the chapter: half-step 0.067, input RMS 0.5, per-term bound 0.0335, N=4,096, totals 137.2 and 2.14, ratio 64. No other quantities are labelled. | Left-to-right flow: embedding enters residual stream; each block reads the stream through layer norm, computes an output, and adds it back. At layer norm, perturbation δ is decomposed: first term removes mean δ; second term removes the component along z; remaining perturbation is orthogonal to the constant vector and z, with norm at most ||δ||/σ. Labels μ, σ, δ, Δz, and ||δ||/σ come from the chapter. The figure does not label quantization error magnitudes or GPTQ/AWQ parameters. | Two side-by-side block layouts. Left: one group containing the outlier 4.0 sets m=4.0 and step 2*4/15=0.533, so 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 all collapse to 0.2667. Right: the outlier is its own block; the other three weights get m=0.3 and step 0.04, giving finer resolution. Labels are the weights, group scale m, and step from the chapter; no axis is needed. | Left panel is a flow: activation channel j and weight column j are rescaled by s=0.1 and 1/s=10, becoming ≈1 and ≈1 while the product stays 1; per-token scaling gives each token its own activation scale. Right panel is a comparison: keys are quantized per-channel, values per-token, because the axis you can average over decides the format. All labelled quantities (10, 0.1, s=0.1, 1/s=10, product 1) appear in the chapter.
